name: CD-FSOD
description: In this paper, we propose a study of the cross-domain few-shot object detection (CD-FSOD) benchmark, consisting of image data from a diverse data domain. On the proposed benchmark, we evaluate state-of-art FSOD approaches, including meta-learning FSOD approaches and fine-tuning FSOD approaches. The results show that these methods tend to fall, and even underperform the naive fine-tuning model. We analyze the reasons for their failure and introduce a strong baseline that uses a mutually-beneficial manner to alleviate the overfitting problem. Our approach is remarkably superior to existing approaches by significant margins (2.0\% on average) on the proposed benchmark. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/FSOD/CD-FSOD}.
reputation: A respected benchmark within the few-shot object detection community for studying cross-domain generalization, though less widely adopted than large-scale detection benchmarks like COCO.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; cross-domain setup can suffer from small target-domain sample sizes and domain shift; possible class imbalance and dataset-specific biases.
